name: Richard Melkonian
paragraphs: Richard Melkonian is an award-winning London based Armenian-British composer and director who works across concert music, opera, theatre, film and performance art. In 2019 he was one of the Old Vic 12 and finished his MA in Opera Making at Guildhall School for Music & Drama in association with the Royal Opera House. His music investigates his dual heritage, blending the rich Armenian folk and liturgical tradition with a contemporary and British sensibility.
Richard's primary practice is a narrative filmmaker who uses his own classical scores. His debut feature length film Universe25 premiered at Slamdance 2025 in Los Angeles.

His last film Fourteen, starring Babirye Bukilwa and Ben Mushumani, premiered at Palm Springs 2020. In 2017, his first film November, starring Andre Flynn, was nominated for best experimental short at Blow Up ArtHouse Festival, Chicago.

In 2018, his commission by Mahogany Group to write new operatic work, The Finding, with libretto by Zoe Palmer was performed at the Institute of Contemporary Arts, London. In 2015, he won the Mary Ryan Award for composition and was also a finalist for the AGBU Sayat Nova Competition where his piece Andastan was performed at Symphony Space, New York. He has written scores for several films including Filip Firlej’s award-winning If It Be Love, premiered at the Raindance Film Festival, London 2015, Emma Swinton’s Isabella, and Aaron Leaman’s documentary Looking for Infinity: El Camino.

For theatre, he was Musical Director at The National Theatre, Cardiff for 'Hail, Cremation! directed by Adele Thomas in 2020. He composed original music for the world premiere of Arthur Miller’s No Villain at Trafalgar Studios in 2016, directed by Sean Turner. He has collaborated with Arab writers Ahmed Masoud as well as Sevan K. Greene on several plays including Nahda, part of Shubbak festival for contemporary Arab arts and literature. As a performance artist, he has performed at the Chalton Gallery and for London’s Art Night at Arnold Circus. Richard also works as a music producer and has collaborated with breakthrough artist Jordan Rakei on their duo project Kwalia with their first EP Pursuit soaring to the top of Spotify’s New Releases chart and playlists. His undergraduate degree and Masters in Classical Composition at the Guildhall was made possible by the Guildhall Scholarship Trust. Alongside composition, Richard also studied Jazz Piano with Barry Green.

name: Giacomo Gex
paragraphs: Giacomo Gex is a British and French actor and director. Born in London, raised in the Sinai desert of Egypt and the Mediterranean island of Ibiza in Spain. At 13 after seeing The Matrix for the first time he became completely absorbed and consumed by cinema. During his teenage years he starred yearly as the lead in his school plays and the gift of a small camcorder spawned his obsession with the art of visual storytelling. After finishing school he attended the Lee Strasberg Theatre and Film Institute in Los Angeles and later New York City. It was there that he began to learn his craft as an actor on stage under such acclaimed teachers as Lola Cohen and Robert Ellerman. As a filmmaker he also made a series of short films and in 2015, Repoman, his short documentary premiered at the renowned Sheffield DocFest as well as the Slamdance Film Festival.

Since moving back to London in 2020 he was selected for his first role in a feature film, Miss Willoughby and the Haunted Bookshop playing a younger version of, and starring alongside, Kelsey Grammer known for such TV shows as Frasier. Towards the end of 2021 Giacomo began work behind the camera on his latest feature film Universe25 for director Richard Melkonian and would soon move in front of the camera playing the lead role as Mott the angel. At the time of the EPK, Giacomo was writing his first feature film script set in the Sinai desert where he grew up and had completed his debut feature documentary, more than seven years in the making, with a world premiere scheduled for the Thessaloniki International Documentary Festival in March 2025.

name: Elodie Chiper
paragraphs: Elodie Chiper is a theatre and film production & costume designer based in London. She graduated in 2020 from The Royal Central School of Speech and Drama London from MFA Scenography. She did her BA in theatre and film set and costume design at The National University of Theatre and Film "I.L. Caragiale" in Bucharest, Romania. In 2021 she was shortlisted for the prestigious The Linbury Prize for Stage and Costume Design for theatre and performance (in partnership with The National Theatre London). She has worked as an Assistant Designer for Hackney Empire, Shotgun Carousel, English Touring Opera, National Theatre of Catalunia, Stuttgart State Opera, collaborated closely with choreographer Yoann Bourgeois as a storyboard artist and worked as a production & costume designer on various short & feature films. She has also been working as an illustrator & graphic artist, collaborating with film magazines such as Films in Frame and publishing houses as Casa de Editura Max Blecher.

Her illustrations also appeared in a special number in the renowned Romanian cultural magazine Steaua and Scena9, accompanying the poems of award winning poet Radu Nitescu. In 2021 she was commissioned by Independent Theatre Timisoara to create an online comic book based on a new writing text by Andrei Ursu. Her own video work and interest for moving image has been shown at film festivals such as Short to the Point Bucharest Experimental film festival and Venice International Film Festival. In 2021 she collaborated with Latvian-Russian poet Sergej Timofejev, member of Orbita, a creative collective of Russian poets and artists and musician Stephane Argillet Stereovoid creating a video poem for one of his poems which was screened at The Brasov European Poetry Biennale.

name: Juanjo L. Salazar
paragraphs: Juanjo L. Salazar is a Colombian-born cinematographer currently based in London and represented by United Talent Agency.
His passion for filmmaking began at a young age when he started experimenting with video cameras, initially filming short home videos and later shooting skate videos for his local skate shop.

While pursuing a BA in Telecommunications Engineering at the Polytechnic University of Barcelona, he developed an interest in camera engineering, which merged his technical and creative backgrounds. After graduating as an engineer and completing an internship at Service Vision in Barcelona, he discovered that cinematography was his true calling.

Since then, he has worked to maintain a diverse portfolio, shifting between narrative, commercial, documentary, music video, and experimental projects. Although primarily focused on short-form work, his collaboration with Richard Melkonian on Universe25 marked a significant step toward longer-format storytelling.
